items.title: Dorothy Donegan — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I used to see Fats Waller and Earl Hines. And I used to hear him play at the Grand Terrace

ctx.x: And where in your neighborhood, where would music be played?

On 42nd Street. We’d play at the DeLisa, and we played at the Allstars. And then there was the Grand Terrace where Earl Hines played. Then there were some sewers around 47th Street where Dan Grissom played and Howlin’ Wolf, and people like that would play.

items.title: Dorothy Donegan — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: He used to play, you could hear him in the alley. “Fatha’ Hines, Fatha’ Hines.” So I would try to mimic him.

ctx.x: Tell me about this broadcast from the Grand Terrace.
He used to play, you could hear him in the alley. “Fatha’ Hines, Fatha’ Hines.” So I would try to mimic him.
And how old were you at the time?
